content.value_statement: Frontend projects need consistent API and form types. This skill guides TypeScript interface, union, generic, and naming patterns from the existing frontend.
actual_capabilities: Defines conventions for user, task, API response, authentication, error, UI, import, and export types.
Explains when to use interfaces, union types, generics, optional properties, and index signatures.
Shows how API response types match backend snake_case fields.
Shows how form data can use frontend-friendly field names.
Provides a complete category type example from entity to API client usage.
limitations: Does not inspect a live backend schema.
Assumes shared frontend types belong in frontend/types/index.ts.
Examples focus on a todo application domain.

use_cases.title: Add New Entity Types
use_cases.description: Frontend developers can model a new backend entity with response, form data, and query parameter types.

use_cases.title: Review API Contract Shapes
use_cases.description: Full-stack engineers can compare backend field names with frontend type definitions before wiring API calls.

use_cases.title: Standardize Component Props
use_cases.description: UI engineers can define props and state types that follow existing names and optional fields.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Entity Types
prompt_templates.prompt: Create frontend TypeScript types for a new entity named Project. Follow the frontend-types skill patterns and explain required versus optional fields.

prompt_templates.title: Align Forms With API Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare my API response fields and form fields for Task. Recommend TypeScript types that keep API fields exact and form fields easy to use.

prompt_templates.title: Design Paginated API Types
prompt_templates.prompt: Design reusable response and query parameter types for a paginated list of categories. Use generics and optional query fields.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Type Coverage Across Features
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these planned frontend features and identify missing entity, form data, query parameter, response, error, and UI state types.

output_examples.input: A request to add frontend types for categories.
output_examples.output: The skill would suggest an entity shape, editable form fields, query parameters, and API usage guidance that matches existing naming rules.

output_examples.input: A request to type a paginated task list response.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend a reusable pagination wrapper, a typed data collection, and metadata fields for page counts and limits.

output_examples.input: A request to review login and session types.
output_examples.output: The skill would check that authentication responses include success state, token data, user data, and session expiration fields.

best_practices: Keep API response types aligned with backend field names.
Use form data types for editable fields instead of reusing full API entities.
Define reusable generics for common response and pagination shapes.
anti_patterns: Do not rename API response fields in shared response types.
Do not make every form field required when the UI can submit partial data.
Do not use broad any types for API responses, errors, or form values.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create frontend TypeScript types for API data, forms, queries, responses, authentication, errors, and UI state.

faq.question: Does it change project files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples for creating or reviewing frontend type definitions.

faq.question: Why keep API response fields in snake_case?
faq.answer: The skill recommends matching backend responses exactly, so API contracts stay clear and predictable.

faq.question: Can form data use camelCase?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill recommends frontend-friendly form field names when data is converted before API calls.

faq.question: Does it support generic response types?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows reusable API and pagination response patterns with generic type parameters.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks the skill as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
